items.title: Finding the Surface Area of a Right Rectangular Prism Given Its Dimensions

sections.normalized_html: A right rectangular prism has dimensions of [MATH: 4] inches by [MATH: 6] inches by [MATH: 10] inches. What is the surface area, in square inches, of the prism?
sections.readable_text: A right rectangular prism has dimensions of [MATH: 4] inches by [MATH: 6] inches by [MATH: 10] inches. What is the surface area, in square inches, of the prism?

sections.normalized_html:
To find the surface area [MATH: A] of a right rectangular prism, we use the formula [MATH: A = 2(\ell w + \ell h + w h),]

where [MATH: \ell,] [MATH: w,] and [MATH: h] are the length, width, and height of the prism.

Substituting the given values [MATH: \ell = 4,] [MATH: w = 6,] and [MATH: h = 10,] we get [MATH: A|= 2(4 ⋅ 6 + 4 ⋅ 10 + 6 ⋅ 10); = 2(24 + 40 + 60); = 2 ⋅ 124; = 248.]

So, the surface area of the prism is [MATH: 248] square inches.
